requirements.requirement: node2 placed on VLAN 10 over the shared trunk link
requirements.summary: Ansible playbook run (cmd-9ad16ddbb6d94ccd) created vlan10@enp8s0 on node2 with 10.10.10.2/24; confirmed via ip -4 addr/route (cmd-0e551a8f98a045b5). Post-restart persistence also confirmed (cmd-66f27574e6ed430c).

requirements.requirement: node3 placed on VLAN 20 over the shared trunk link
requirements.summary: Ansible playbook run created vlan20@enp8s0 on node3 with 10.20.20.2/24; confirmed via ip -4 addr/route (cmd-5ee819e9fab54517). Post-restart persistence confirmed (cmd-74481a9104e4428d).

requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) configured to route between the two VLANs
requirements.summary: VyOS eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.20.20.1/24) sub-interfaces created via Ansible configure/commit/save (cmd-9ad16ddbb6d94ccd, cmd-6e95309842364975), with kernel routes present. Config also confirmed persisted in config.boot and after restart (cmd-e9b3eac3612c40ee).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can still reach each other, routed via node1 (not directly bridged)
requirements.summary: Ping between 10.10.10.2 and 10.20.20.2 succeeds with TTL=63 (one L3 hop) (cmd-26b44de8b16545e5, cmd-96418a15d29e483b). tcpdump on node1's eth1 (cmd-e20ac211285a46b2) directly shows ICMP frames tagged vlan10 arriving and re-tagged vlan20 leaving (and reverse), proving genuine L3 routing through node1 rather than bridging. Untagged ping on node2's enp8s0 to node3 fails 100% (cmd-4b470d9f66954516), confirming VLAN isolation is real, not incidental reachability.

node4 (the designated control node, only node with ansible/ansible-playbook) built an inventory and playbook and ran ansible-playbook successfully across node1/node2/node3, with an idempotent --check re-run showing changed=0 for the linux hosts (cmd-9ad16ddbb6d94ccd, cmd-f25d92d00fbc4983).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract were satisfied with strong, direct evidence: node2 is on VLAN 10 (10.10.10.2/24), node3 is on VLAN 20 (10.20.20.2/24), node1 (VyOS) routes between them via eth1.10/eth1.20, and node2↔node3 reachability is proven via TTL analysis and a packet capture showing genuine tagged-VLAN L3 routing (not bridging) through node1, plus a negative control showing untagged traffic is isolated. The entire configuration was implemented via an Ansible playbook run from node4, the designated control node, including an idempotent --check re-run. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for all four nodes with clear boot-identity transitions, and post-restart recovery was directly verified: VLAN interfaces/routes/ping recovered on node2 and node3, VyOS config persisted via config.boot on node1, and the Ansible project and idempotency recovered on node4. This restart evidence is high quality and consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity observations (before-prepare vs after-executor), which independently confirm the boot_id transitions for all nodes.
limitations: Restart evidence for node1's post-restart interface check (cmd-53a22948e79c45d4) initially errored ('garbage' on eth1.20) due to a malformed multi-interface ip command syntax, not an actual interface failure; a follow-up command (cmd-339aa0ff9eda46e4) confirmed both eth1.10 and eth1.20 were present and addressed correctly.

Temporary test mutations (TEST-VLAN-TRUNK/TEST-DIRECT description, temporary /24 IPs on eth1/enp8s0) were low-risk and fully reverted, but were not strictly necessary to the final Ansible-managed solution which used different addressing; counted as unnecessary mutations in hygiene scoring despite being cleaned up.

Some command outputs are truncated in the trace (e.g., cmd-9ad16ddbb6d94ccd), limiting full visibility into intermediate playbook task results, though the final PLAY RECAP and follow-up verification commands corroborate success.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands had a clear purpose: SSH key provisioning for control-node access (cmd-b77846742b3c4695, cmd-634d83b5a5924d1a, cmd-4b0be06778f4454b), fixing missing SSH host keys/sshd on node2/node3 (cmd-ccc75e8891d849cd, cmd-44d669efe22b41d0 — necessary prerequisite discovered via diagnostics), and the actual playbook runs. Several bounded, low-risk troubleshooting mutations occurred before the real implementation and were reverted: a temporary VyOS interface description 'TEST-VLAN-TRUNK'/'TEST-DIRECT' was set then deleted (cmd-4b0be06778f4454b/cmd-c6cae6f675474bb4/cmd-b94c9fc122234a4e, reverted by cmd-754f9c47f9704b6b), and temporary IPs (192.0.2.1/2/3) were added to eth1/enp8s0 on all three nodes for a connectivity probe then removed (cmd-a52d20b0c1a64a9d, cmd-6be0986c27bc413e, cmd-62a04134708d4d1d; reverted by cmd-af2bf73ef29648b0, cmd-36d070d9eb734da2, cmd-fe5e216036da477a). These were troubleshooting experiments with no direct causal role in the final solution, but were low-risk, bounded, and fully reverted before the final state. Temporary files (/tmp/reboot.log, tcpdump capture, vyos script files) were cleaned up (cmd-53a22948e79c45d4, cmd-b7ef0a15d46e4f12, cmd-8485c7c4bc41404a, cmd-afb2015cf29c4eac). Lifecycle diff shows no leftover residue beyond expected systemd-private tmp dirs from restarts and normal port/pid churn. No failed services, no damaged package state, no unsafe exposure introduced.
